segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinegrower.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away, and every branch that does bear fruit he prunes clean so that it may bear more fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, is the one who bears much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone does not remain in me, that person is thrown out like a branch and withers; such branches are gathered, thrown into the fire, and burned.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask for whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In this my Father is glorified: that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you. Remain in my love.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have spoken these things to you so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be made full.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This is my commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No one has greater love than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are my friends if you do what I command you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I no longer call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I heard from my Father I have made known to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit, and for your fruit to remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: These things I command you so that you will love one another.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world—that is why the world hates you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘A slave is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will also keep yours.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But they will do all these things to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever hates me hates my Father too.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would have no sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But this happened so that the word written in their Law might be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who comes out from the Father—he will testify about me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And you also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.

notes.note: In Israel’s Scriptures the vine or vineyard is a standing image for Israel itself, planted and tended by God and often faulted for failing to yield good fruit (for example Psalm 80 and Isaiah 5). A first-century Jewish reader would hear “the true vine” against that background. The speech continues from chapter 14 and runs on into chapter 16, so the quotation marks do not close at the end of this chapter.

The verb can mean either “remove” or “lift up,” and a minority of interpreters think the vinegrower is lifting trailing branches off the ground so that they can bear. Most scholars take it as removal, which fits the discarded and burned branches of verse 6. That is the reading followed here.

The Greek verb means “to clean” and was used for clearing or pruning plants. It echoes “takes away” in sound (airei, kathairei), and it leads straight into “you are already clean” (katharoi) in verse 3. Most versions have simply “prunes,” which hides the link; “prunes clean” keeps the connection visible.

The traditional “abide” is now rare outside religious language. The Greek is the ordinary verb for staying or remaining somewhere, and “remain” is used for it throughout this chapter, including for the fruit in verse 16. Several modern versions do the same; others keep “abide.”

notes.traditional: so prove to be my disciples
notes.note: The verb ordinarily means “become,” but it can also mean “turn out to be,” and many versions render “prove to be my disciples,” since the hearers already are disciples. Manuscripts are also divided between “and become” and “and you will become.” The plainer “become” is kept here; on this reading discipleship is something one keeps growing into.

The Greek word denotes a slave, a person owned by a master, not a hired servant. The contrast depends on this: a slave is given orders without explanations, while a friend is taken into confidence. Many traditional versions have “servants”; a number of recent ones use “slaves.”

notes.phrase: so that you will love one another
notes.traditional: These things I command you, that ye love one another
notes.note: The Greek can be read as giving the purpose of the commands (“I command you these things so that you will love one another”) or their content (“This is what I command you: love one another”). The plural “these things” slightly favors the first reading, which is followed here. Verse 12 clearly uses the same construction for content, and several versions take this verse that way as well.
The Greek form can be a command (“know”) or a statement (“you know”). Most modern versions take it as a command, as here.

The words quoted come from the Psalms (see Psalms 35:19 and 69:4), not from the books of Moses. “Law” is used here in the broad sense, current at the time, of the Scriptures as a whole. “Their Law” points out that the Scripture the opponents themselves claim testifies against them.

The traditional “Comforter” goes back to early English versions. Outside the New Testament the word is used of someone who speaks on another’s behalf, and 1 John 2:1 clearly uses it that way. That sense fits the testifying role described here. “Advocate,” “Helper,” and “Counselor” are all in current use among translations.

The Greek form can be a statement (“you are testifying”) or a command (“you too must testify”), and versions differ; some render it as a future. The English here is left open in the same way as the Greek.

candidates.reason: A theme word in John and 1 John that versions split between “abide” and “remain”; varying it would obscure the thread.
Recurs across the whole New Testament and is rendered “servant,” “slave,” or “bondservant”; the choice affects the parables, Paul’s self-descriptions, and the household codes.
Frequent in John, Acts, and Revelation and rendered variously “testify,” “bear witness,” or “witness”; it needs one choice coordinated with μαρτυρία and μάρτυς.
Versions vary between “command” and “commandment” for the same sense, and John’s argument links Jesus’ commandments with the Father’s.
It overlaps with ἀγαπάω, and a policy is needed on whether the two verbs are distinguished in English, especially for John 21.
